does: Boils a liquid down, so that its water leaves as steam and what remains is thicker and stronger.

intro.what: Reducing boils liquid uncovered so that water leaves as steam and the liquid grows thicker and stronger.
intro.why: It teaches you to connect evaporation with flavour and texture, and to season after concentrating a sauce.

how: Use a wide pan. The wider the surface, the faster the water leaves.
Watch the level against the side of the pan, and the size of the bubbles.
Stop when it coats the back of a spoon, and season only then.

cues.text: The bubbles grow larger and slower, and a finger drawn across the back of a coated spoon leaves a clear path.
The boil deepens from a rattle to a slow, thick plop.

mistakes.mistake: Salting before reducing, so that the salt is concentrated with everything else.
Walking away near the end, when a sauce goes from syrup to scorched in moments.
mistakes.fix: Stay with it once it starts to thicken, and pull it off the heat early.

quiz.question: What happens to a liquid as it reduces?
choices: It becomes thicker and stronger as water leaves.
It keeps the same strength while its colour changes.
quiz.because: Water leaves as steam, so the remaining liquid becomes more concentrated and thicker.

quiz.question: Which pan setup helps liquid reduce?
choices: A wide pan under a tight lid.
A wide pan, boiling steadily without a lid.
quiz.because: A wide surface lets water leave faster. Keeping the pan uncovered lets the steam escape.

quiz.question: What spoon test helps you judge whether the sauce has thickened?
choices: A finger leaves a clear path across the back of a coated spoon.
The liquid looks exactly as thin as at the start.
The spoon emerges without any coating.
quiz.because: A coating that holds a clear path across the spoon shows the sauce has thickened.

quiz.question: A reduced sauce tastes too salty. What would you change next time?
choices: Season to the final taste before starting to boil.
Season at the end of the reduction.
Cover the pan to keep all the water in.
quiz.because: Salt concentrates along with the sauce. Season after reducing so you judge the concentrated liquid.

comes_after.why: A pan sauce is deglazed first and reduced second.
A cook who can hold a simmer can judge a boil that must not scorch.
